name: ListDetail
intent: A list with the picked record beside it: a ListView on one side and the record in a pane on the other, or one at a time on a phone.
usage: Use ListDetail when people go through records one after another without leaving the list: an invoice queue, an inbox, approvals. It is a blueprint: it composes kit pieces and keeps no state of its own. list is a kit ListView, usually with selection single and interaction drill; its onOpen tells the screen which record is open. detail is that record, built from kit Sections, FormDisplay and Tables; title names it and actions puts its Buttons at the end of the pane's header. open says a record is open. empty shows in the pane when none is, usually a kit Empty. The list can be any ListView: grouped by status under headers that fold, the inbox template with avatars, unread dots and status lines, or rows with a More menu; the pane works the same. When records sit under other records, give the ListView items with children: the list steps into them in place, with Back, and a leaf opens beside it, like accounts that hold their invoices. layout sets where the record goes: side puts it in a pane beside the list, stacked puts it under the whole list, and inline opens it right under its row, inside the list. With side, the frame measures its own width: from 640 up the list and the pane sit side by side (two fifths and three fifths); below, the list shows until a record opens, then the pane covers it with a Back button that calls onBack, named by backLabel. The page's name and trail are the kit PageHeader in the AppShell page around it. See contracts/listdetail.json for the full contract.

detail.note: The open record: kit Sections, FormDisplay, Tables.

open.note: A record is open. On a phone the pane then covers the list.

title.note: The open record's name, the pane's heading.

actions.note: Buttons for the open record, at the end of the pane's header.

empty.note: What the pane shows when no record is open, usually a kit Empty.

onBack.note: The phone's Back button. Close the record here.

backLabel.note: Names the Back button, like Back to invoices.

layout.note: side: the list and the pane side by side, one at a time on a phone. stacked: the list on top and the record under it. inline: the record opens right under its row, inside the list; it needs a ListView with selection single, and empty does not show.

label.note: Names the list and pane together for screen readers.

useWhen: Going through records one after another: an invoice queue, an inbox, approvals.
A record short enough to read in a pane beside the list.
A list that must stay in view while its records are read.
Records under other records, like an account's invoices: a nested ListView steps in, and the leaf opens beside it.
A long queue split by status: a grouped ListView keeps what needs attention on top.
Stacked when the list is short and the record needs the full width; inline when people read one record at a time and want the rest of the list to stay in place around it.
doNot: Do not add state to it; it is a blueprint. The screen keeps which record is open.
Do not use it for records with a lot to show or edit. Drill into a RecordPage instead.
Do not build the list inside it. Pass a kit ListView.
Do not put the page's name inside it. That is the PageHeader in the frame around it.
a11y: The list and pane together are a region named after label, with a hidden h2 of the same name so headings stay in order; the open record is a region named after title with its own h2.
On a phone the Back button is named by backLabel and returns to the list.
Picking a row keeps focus in the list, so people can go through records with the keyboard.
snippet:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number} actions={<Button size="sm">Download</Button>}
  list={<ListView label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill" selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId} items={invoices} />}
  empty={<Empty icon="receipt_long" title="Pick an invoice" />}
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: A record open
examples.usage: An invoice queue with one invoice open beside the list. Pick another row and the pane follows.

examples.title: Nothing open yet
examples.usage: Before a row is picked, the pane shows an Empty that says what to do.

examples.title: Grouped by status
examples.usage: The queue split under Needs Attention, Open and Paid. Headers fold their rows away and stay on top while the list scrolls.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      groups={[{ id: "attention", title: "Needs Attention" }, { id: "open", title: "Open" }, { id: "paid", title: "Paid" }]}
      collapsible stickyGroups
      items={invoices} selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: Inbox template
examples.usage: Each row shows the account's avatar, an unread dot on what changed, and a status line under the text, so the queue reads like an inbox.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      items={[{ id: "INV-1042", primary: "INV-1042", secondary: "Apex Digital Services · $4,820.00", avatar: "Apex Digital Services", unread: true, message: "Card declined, retry on Friday", messageTone: "danger", badge: "Overdue", badgeTone: "danger" }, …]}
      selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: Row actions
examples.usage: Every invoice action sits behind one More button on its row, the same menu as the list on ListPage. View invoice opens it beside the list.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      items={invoices.map((inv) => ({ ...inv, menu: invoiceMenu }))}
      onAction={(id, action) => { if (action === "view") setOpenId(id); }}
      selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: Nested list
examples.usage: Accounts hold their invoices. A click on an account steps into its invoices in place, with Back to the accounts; a click on an invoice opens it beside the list. Here the list is stepped into Apex with INV-1042 open.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Accounts" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      items={accounts} path={path} onPathChange={setPath}
      selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: Invoices under their account
examples.usage: The list starts at the accounts. A click opens an account's invoices right under it, indented, and a click on an invoice opens it beside the list. Here Apex is open with INV-1042 showing.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      nesting="expand" items={accounts} expanded={expanded} onExpandedChange={setExpanded}
      selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: Record under the list
examples.usage: layout stacked: the whole list on top and the open record under it, each the full width.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" layout="stacked" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      items={invoices} selected={openId ? [openId] : []} onOpen={setOpenId}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>

examples.title: Record under its row
examples.usage: layout inline: the record opens right under the row that was picked, inside the list, and the rows after it move down. A click on the open row closes it.
examples.code:
<ListDetail
  label="Invoices" layout="inline" open={Boolean(invoice)} onBack={() => setOpenId(null)} backLabel="Back to invoices"
  title={invoice?.number}
  list={
    <ListView
      label="Invoices" selection="single" interaction="drill"
      items={invoices} selected={openId ? [openId] : []}
      onOpen={(id) => setOpenId(id === openId ? null : id)}
    />
  }
  detail={invoice && <Section title="Invoice Details">…</Section>}
/>
